## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Satadhammajātaka* (Ja 179) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, it is situated as the ninth story of its chapter and opens with the verse lemma *Tañ ca appan ti* [Fausböll 1879]. The introductory setting (*paccuppannavatthu*) locates the teaching while the Buddha was residing at Jetavana, delivered in response to monks who had adopted twenty-one unlawful or improper ways of earning a livelihood (*ekavīsatividhā anesanā*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].

In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), the young high-born brahmin Satadhamma (*Satadhammad-māṇava*), driven by desperate starvation, eats leftovers cast aside by an outcaste (*caṇḍālucchiṭṭhaka*) [Fausböll 1879]. Tormented by intense shame and remorse, he vomits blood, abandons society for the forest, and dies a destitute death [Fausböll 1879]. The Buddha compares Satadhamma's desolation upon consuming illicit food to the spiritual fate of a monk living off wrongful gains, noting that forbidden livelihoods can bring no genuine joy or happiness [Fausböll 1879]. Following this exposition and the teaching of the Four Noble Truths, numerous monks attain the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*), and the Buddha reveals that he was the young outcaste (*caṇḍālaputta*) in that former life [Fausböll 1879].

Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates four matching passages (315 characters) shared between the canonical text and the commentary in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match §2.1–3.1 with §503–505_0) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Tibetan, or Chinese Āgama literature [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
